Let $Q_2=\mathbb C^2$ be the ordered qubit register with computational basis
$(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, and use the ordered two-factor register
$Q_2\otimes Q_2$ from [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. Define the
four **Bell vectors** by

$$|\Phi^+\rangle:=\frac{|00\rangle+|11\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Phi^-\rangle:=\frac{|00\rangle-|11\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Psi^+\rangle:=\frac{|01\rangle+|10\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Psi^-\rangle:=\frac{|01\rangle-|10\rangle}{\sqrt2}.$$

The ordered label convention is
$|00\rangle\mapsto|\Phi^+\rangle$,
$|01\rangle\mapsto|\Psi^+\rangle$,
$|10\rangle\mapsto|\Phi^-\rangle$, and
$|11\rangle\mapsto|\Psi^-\rangle$. Thus the first label is the phase/sign
bit and the second is the bit-flip bit. The next theorem verifies that these
vectors form an orthonormal basis and gives the corresponding preparation and
decoding maps.

In the computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, use $X,Y,Z$ from [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]] and define
$$H:=\frac{X+Z}{\sqrt2}=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad S:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&i\end{pmatrix},\qquad T:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&e^{i\pi/4}\end{pmatrix}.$$
The phases displayed in these matrices are exact; they are not identified modulo a scalar when the matrices are later placed under a control.

For real $\theta$ and a real unit vector $\mathbf n=(n_x,n_y,n_z)$, define the axis rotation
$$R_{\mathbf n}(\theta):=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\theta}{2}\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\right),\qquad R_z(\theta):=R_{(0,0,1)}(\theta).$$
Here $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ and $\|\mathbf n\|_2$ have the meanings fixed in [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]]. For a bounded endomorphism $B$ of $Q_2$, the notation $\exp(B)$ means the operator-norm series $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}B^k/k!$ of [[lem-exponential-series-of-a-bounded-operator]] at scalar parameter $1$. Its convergence applies here because $Q_2$ is finite-dimensional and complete and every linear endomorphism of $Q_2$ is bounded ([[cor-finite-dimensional-normed-spaces-are-banach]], [[cor-linear-maps-with-finite-dimensional-domain-are-bounded]]).

The unitary identities for the fixed matrices are verified below. The following theorem proves the closed form and unitarity of each $R_{\mathbf n}(\theta)$.

In the ordered two-qubit basis $|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$, the controlled-NOT with first wire control and second wire target is

$$\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}|a,t\rangle=|a,t\mathbin{\oplus}a\rangle,\qquad a,t\in\{0,1\}.$$

Equivalently, it is the control block $C(X)=\operatorname{diag}(I,X)$ of [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]], where $X$ is the Pauli bit-flip matrix. The wire order is part of the definition.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

For every $d\ge1$, the ordered computational basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of
the register $Q_d$ from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]] is an
orthonormal basis for its declared inner product. Separately, the one-dimensional
zero-qubit register has the basis $\{1\}$ by definition.

For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

Let $V,W$ be inner product spaces ([[def-inner-product-space]]) over the same field and let $T:V\to W$ be linear ([[def-linear-map]]). An **adjoint** of $T$ is a linear map $T^*:W\to V$ such that

$$\langle Tv,w\rangle_W=\langle v,T^*w\rangle_V$$

for every $v\in V$ and $w\in W$. Existence is not part of the definition; in finite dimensions it will follow from Riesz representation.

Let $T:V\to W$ be a linear map between finite-dimensional inner product spaces. In orthonormal bases $\mathcal E=(e_j)$ of $V$ and $\mathcal F=(f_i)$ of $W$,

$$[T^*]_{\mathcal E\leftarrow\mathcal F}=\overline{[T]_{\mathcal F\leftarrow\mathcal E}}^{\mathsf T}.$$

Over $\mathbb R$ this is the transpose. The statement includes zero-sized bases.

derivations.claim: The matrix in [F2] gives $H|a\rangle=(|0\rangle+(-1)^a|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ for each bit $a$. By [F6], $(H\otimes I)|ab\rangle=(|0,b\rangle+(-1)^a|1,b\rangle)/\sqrt2$.

From [F3], applying CNOT twice fixes every basis vector because $(t\oplus a)\oplus a=t$. Its matrix permutes the orthonormal basis [F4], so its inverse is its transpose and equals itself. The matrix of $H\otimes I$ in [F4] is real symmetric and its square is the identity by [F2]. Thus both factors are self-adjoint involutions, and direct composition gives $(H\otimes I)\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}B=I=B(H\otimes I)\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}$.

Apply the control-first action in [F3] to the two terms of step 1.1. The control-zero term is fixed, while the control-one term changes its target from $b$ to $b\oplus1$. Therefore $B|ab\rangle=(|0,b\rangle+(-1)^a|1,b\oplus1\rangle)/\sqrt2$.

Substituting $00,01,10,11$ into step 2.1 gives $\Phi^+,\Psi^+,\Phi^-,\Psi^-$ in that order, exactly as defined in [F1]. Each has norm one because it is a signed sum of two distinct orthonormal computational basis vectors from [F5], divided by $\sqrt2$. The inner product of $\Phi^+$ with $\Phi^-$ and of $\Psi^+$ with $\Psi^-$ is $(1-1)/2=0$; cross-pair inner products are zero because their computational supports are disjoint.
The four vectors in step 3.1 are an orthonormal set of four vectors in the four-dimensional space whose product basis is listed in [F4]; hence they are an orthonormal basis.

In matrices, $(AB)_{ij}=\sum_k A_{ik}B_{kj}$, so conjugating and transposing this finite sum gives $(AB)^\dagger=B^\dagger A^\dagger$. By [F7]–[F8] this is the adjoint product rule in the register pairing. Since both factors in [F6] and [F3] are self-adjoint by step 1.2, $B^\dagger=(H\otimes I)\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}$. Applying CNOT sends the four Bell vectors to $\frac{|0\rangle+|1\rangle}{\sqrt2}\otimes|0\rangle$, $\frac{|0\rangle+|1\rangle}{\sqrt2}\otimes|1\rangle$, $\frac{|0\rangle-|1\rangle}{\sqrt2}\otimes|0\rangle$, and $\frac{|0\rangle-|1\rangle}{\sqrt2}\otimes|1\rangle$, respectively. By the matrix in [F2], $H$ sends the first factors in these expressions to $|0\rangle,|0\rangle,|1\rangle,|1\rangle$, respectively, so the reverse sequence recovers $00,01,10,11$.

The **teleportation procedure** has input a normalized qubit vector $|\psi\rangle_A\in Q_2$ and a preshared resource $|\Phi^+\rangle_{BC}$, with Alice holding wires $A,B$ and Bob holding $C$. The wire order is $A,B,C$. It uses $|\Phi^+\rangle$ from [[def-qc-bell-basis]], CNOT with $A$ control and $B$ target from [[def-qc-cnot-and-control-target-order]], the Hadamard $H$ from [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]], the Pauli matrices from [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]], and the finite projective measurement convention of [[def-qc-projective-measurement]].

1. Alice applies $\operatorname{CNOT}_{A\to B}$ and then $H_A$, so the combined operator is $V_{AB}=(H_A\otimes I_{BC})\operatorname{CNOT}_{A\to B}$, with the rightmost gate applied first.
2. Alice measures $A,B$ in their ordered computational basis and records the pair $(a,b)\in\{0,1\}^2$, in that wire order.
3. Alice sends the two classical bits $a,b$ to Bob.
4. Bob applies $X_C^b$ and then $Z_C^a$, whose operator product is $Z_C^aX_C^b$.

The output is the corrected state on Bob's wire $C$. The shared Bell pair is an
input resource; its preparation and physical realization are outside this
procedure. A zero-probability measurement label has no conditional state and
is assigned no branch output; the normalized-input hypotheses here are later
shown to make all four labels positive.

derivations.claim: By [F2], the initial vector is $2^{-1/2}(\alpha|000\rangle+\alpha|011\rangle+\beta|100\rangle+\beta|111\rangle)$ in wire order $A,B,C$.

Applying [F4] to the four basis vectors gives $2^{-1/2}(\alpha|000\rangle+\alpha|011\rangle+\beta|110\rangle+\beta|101\rangle)$ after CNOT: the first two terms have control bit $0$ and are fixed, while the last two have control bit $1$ and their target bits flip.

By [F3] and [F6], $H_A$ sends each first-wire $|0\rangle$ to $(|0\rangle+|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and each $|1\rangle$ to $(|0\rangle-|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$. Regrouping the resulting eight terms by the first two wires gives $\frac12\bigl(|00\rangle(\alpha|0\rangle+\beta|1\rangle)+|01\rangle(\alpha|1\rangle+\beta|0\rangle)+|10\rangle(\alpha|0\rangle-\beta|1\rangle)+|11\rangle(\alpha|1\rangle-\beta|0\rangle)\bigr)$.

The four receiver vectors in step 3.1 are respectively $|\psi\rangle$, $X|\psi\rangle$, $Z|\psi\rangle$, and $XZ|\psi\rangle$ by the actions in [F5]. These are exactly $X^bZ^a|\psi\rangle$ for labels $00,01,10,11$, so step 3.1 is the sum in the Statement.

For arbitrary $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb C$, put
$|\psi\rangle=\alpha|0\rangle+\beta|1\rangle$ and
$V_{AB}=(H_A\otimes I_{BC})\operatorname{CNOT}_{A\to B}$, in wire order
$A,B,C$. Then

$$V_{AB}(|\psi\rangle_A\otimes|\Phi^+\rangle_{BC})=\frac12\sum_{a,b\in\{0,1\}}|ab\rangle_{AB}\otimes X_C^bZ_C^a|\psi\rangle_C.$$

No normalization assumption on $|\psi\rangle$ is needed for this vector
identity.

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty outcome set ([[def-dimension]], [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]]). Its **endomorphisms** are its complex-linear maps $H\to H$ ([[def-vector-space-of-linear-maps]]); for an endomorphism $P$, $P^*$ denotes its adjoint, which exists uniquely in finite dimension ([[def-adjoint-of-a-linear-map-between-inner-product-spaces]], [[thm-adjoint-exists-and-is-unique-in-finite-dimension]]). A **finite projective measurement** on $H$ with outcomes $\Omega$ is a family $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ of endomorphisms such that

$$P_a^*=P_a,\qquad P_a^2=P_a,\qquad P_aP_b=0\ (a\ne b),\qquad \sum_{a\in\Omega}P_a=I_H.$$

The products above are compositions, the sum is pointwise addition of endomorphisms, and $I_H$ is the identity map; these operations preserve linear maps ([[prop-linear-maps-form-a-vector-space]], [[lem-composition-and-identity-linear-maps]]). The projections $P_a=0$ are permitted. For a density operator $\rho$ on $H$ (nonnegative and trace one, [[def-qc-density-operator]]), the associated outcome weights are $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$; their nonnegativity and normalization are proved in [[thm-qc-projective-measurement-outcome-law]].

Let $\rho$ be a density operator on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $H$, and let $(P_a)_{a\in\Omega}$ be a finite projective measurement on $H$. Then $p_\rho(a)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_a)$ lies in $[0,1]$ for every $a$, and $\sum_{a\in\Omega}p_\rho(a)=1$.

The **dense-coding procedure** takes classical input bits $a,b\in\{0,1\}$ and
a preshared pair $|\Phi^+\rangle_{AB}$, with Alice holding $A$ and Bob holding
$B$. The local convention is that $a$ is the phase bit and $b$ the flip bit.

1. Alice applies $X_A^b$ and then $Z_A^a$, so the encoding operator is $Z_A^aX_A^b$.
2. Alice sends the single qubit $A$ to Bob.
3. Bob applies $\operatorname{CNOT}_{A\to B}$, then $H_A$, and measures the ordered register $A,B$ in the computational basis.
4. Bob outputs the ordered pair of measured bits.

If a surrounding measurement model assigns an outcome zero weight, no
conditional state is assigned for that outcome. For each of the four possible input pairs, the decoded output equals that pair with weight one and the other three outcomes have weight zero, as computed in the correctness theorem.

The Bell resource, Pauli matrices, Hadamard, CNOT wire order, and projective
measurement use the conventions of [[def-qc-bell-basis]],
[[def-qc-pauli-matrices]], [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]],
[[def-qc-cnot-and-control-target-order]], and
[[def-qc-projective-measurement]]. No optimality claim is part of this
procedure.

Let $Q_2=\mathbb C^2$ be the ordered qubit register with computational basis
$(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$, and use the ordered two-factor register

$$|\Phi^+\rangle:=\frac{|00\rangle+|11\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Phi^-\rangle:=\frac{|00\rangle-|11\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Psi^+\rangle:=\frac{|01\rangle+|10\rangle}{\sqrt2},\qquad |\Psi^-\rangle:=\frac{|01\rangle-|10\rangle}{\sqrt2}.$$

The ordered label convention is
$|00\rangle\mapsto|\Phi^+\rangle$,
$|01\rangle\mapsto|\Psi^+\rangle$,
$|10\rangle\mapsto|\Phi^-\rangle$, and
$|11\rangle\mapsto|\Psi^-\rangle$. Thus the first label is the phase/sign
bit and the second is the bit-flip bit. The next theorem verifies that these
vectors form an orthonormal basis and gives the corresponding preparation and
decoding maps.

orthonormal basis of $Q_2\otimes Q_2$, and
$B^\dagger=(H\otimes I)\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}$ maps those four vectors

$$P_a^*=P_a,\qquad P_a^2=P_a,\qquad P_aP_b=0\ (a\ne b),\qquad \sum_{a\in\Omega}P_a=I_H.$$

For a subspace $S\subseteq H$, $\rho$ is **faithful on $S$** when $\operatorname{supp}(\rho)=S$ and the restriction $\rho|_S:S\to S$ is positive definite in the sense of [[def-non-negative-and-positive-operator]]. derivations.claim: Applying $Z_A^aX_A^b$ to $|\Phi^+\rangle=(|00\rangle+|11\rangle)/\sqrt2$ and using [F4] gives the four cases: $00\mapsto\Phi^+$, $01\mapsto\Psi^+$, $10\mapsto\Phi^-$, and $11\mapsto\Psi^-$. In the last case, $Z_A X_A|00\rangle=-|10\rangle$ and $Z_A X_A|11\rangle=|01\rangle$, so the state is exactly $\Psi^-$ in the chosen convention.

For $x\in\{0,1\}$, [F4] gives $Z^a|x\rangle=(-1)^{ax}|x\rangle$. Expanding the left side and then substituting $y=x\oplus b$ gives $(Z^aX^b\otimes I)|\Phi^+\rangle=2^{-1/2}\sum_x(-1)^{a(x\oplus b)}|x\oplus b,x\rangle=2^{-1/2}\sum_y(-1)^{ay}|y,y\oplus b\rangle=(I\otimes X^bZ^a)|\Phi^+\rangle$. The same matrices give $XZ=-ZX$, hence $X^bZ^a=(-1)^{ab}Z^aX^b$. The scalar $\lambda=(-1)^{ab}$ leaves the rank-one projector unchanged because $(\lambda v)(\lambda v)^*=|\lambda|^2vv^*=vv^*$; it changes no projective outcome weight, while the direct four-case vectors in step 1.1 fix the exact label phase.

By [F3], the four encoded vectors in step 1.1 are $B|ab\rangle$, and $B^\dagger$ sends each to $|ab\rangle$. The output projectors are the orthogonal basis projections in [F8]. The rank-one matrix of $|ab\rangle$ has a single diagonal entry $1$ at label $(a,b)$, so its quadratic form is nonnegative and its trace is one by [F7]; it is a density operator by [F9]. Then [F5] and [F7] give weight one at $(a,b)$ and zero at the other labels. By [F6] this is a deterministic output law.

The procedure [F1] begins with one shared pair, sends only wire $A$ once, and outputs the two input bits at Bob's measurement. Its instructions contain at most two conditional Pauli gate occurrences for Alice's encoding, one CNOT and one Hadamard for Bob, and two final measured wires. Thus it achieves the stated resource exchange for this procedure; no optimality statement is used.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

$$\operatorname{supp}(\rho):=\{x\in H: \langle x,y\rangle=0\text{ for every }y\in\ker\rho\}.$$

The **teleportation procedure** has input a normalized qubit vector $|\psi\rangle_A\in Q_2$ and a preshared resource $|\Phi^+\rangle_{BC}$, with Alice holding wires $A,B$ and Bob holding $C$. The wire order is $A,B,C$. It uses $|\Phi^+\rangle$ from [[def-qc-bell-basis]], CNOT with $A$ control and $B$ target from [[def-qc-cnot-and-control-target-order]], the Hadamard $H$ from [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]], the Pauli matrices from [[def-qc-pauli-matrices]], and the finite projective measurement convention of [[def-qc-projective-measurement]].

1. Alice applies $\operatorname{CNOT}_{A\to B}$ and then $H_A$, so the combined operator is $V_{AB}=(H_A\otimes I_{BC})\operatorname{CNOT}_{A\to B}$, with the rightmost gate applied first.
2. Alice measures $A,B$ in their ordered computational basis and records the pair $(a,b)\in\{0,1\}^2$, in that wire order.
3. Alice sends the two classical bits $a,b$ to Bob.
4. Bob applies $X_C^b$ and then $Z_C^a$, whose operator product is $Z_C^aX_C^b$.

The output is the corrected state on Bob's wire $C$. The shared Bell pair is an
input resource; its preparation and physical realization are outside this
procedure. A zero-probability measurement label has no conditional state and
is assigned no branch output; the normalized-input hypotheses here are later
shown to make all four labels positive.

For every normalized input qubit vector $|\psi\rangle$, the projective
measurement of the first two wires after the pre-measurement gates in
[[alg-qc-teleportation]] has
$\Pr[(a,b)]=1/4$ for each $(a,b)\in\{0,1\}^2$.

For every qubit vector $|\psi\rangle$ and bits $a,b\in\{0,1\}$, the
teleportation branch byproduct is $X^bZ^a|\psi\rangle$, and the prescribed
correction returns it exactly:

$$Z^aX^bX^bZ^a|\psi\rangle=|\psi\rangle.$$

The operator order is part of the statement; no Pauli factors are commuted.

Let $R$ be any finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let
$|\Psi\rangle_{AR}$ be any normalized vector on $Q_2\otimes R$, with no
product-state assumption. Run teleportation on $A$ using a shared
$|\Phi^+\rangle_{BC}$, keeping the global wire order $A,B,C,R$ and applying
the canonical ordered tensor identifications. For every measured label $(a,b)$,
the corrected joint vector on $C\otimes R$ is exactly
$|\Psi\rangle_{CR}$, with $A$ relabelled as the output wire $C$.

record with separate coordinates as follows. A **shared-pair use** is one
initial Bell pair supplied as an input resource; its preparation is excluded.
A **classical communication bit** is one bit sent from Alice to Bob; the record
contains two. A **transmitted qubit** is a qubit sent during the protocol after
the shared pair is available; the record contains zero. A **measurement-record
bit** is one of the two ordered computational-basis outcomes measured by Alice;
the record contains two such bits. A **local gate occurrence** is counted by
the size convention of [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]], namely as one
gate occurrence in the declared circuit: Alice uses one CNOT and one Hadamard,
and Bob uses at most two conditional Pauli gate occurrences, $X^b$ and $Z^a$.

counts the stated procedure only; it asserts no optimality or physical
realization.
